rows.text: That flickering mechatron phantom... Is that the secret weapon you used to defeat the Herald of Death fifteen years ago?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Looks like you have a ways to go still, but to think you actually recreated it! My darling fake "daughter," you truly are a fascinating being!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: So the "father" who was with her since she was six, guiding her to reach the stars... that was you all along? A Lord Ravager?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Telling her about the wonders of the cosmos at bedtime, awkwardly trying to calm her when she was crying... Was all of that just an act? Just to play some sick joke?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You look genuinely heartbroken... Have you been playing "Himeko" for so long that you feel you really are her?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Or did you obtain her memories before she died?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: "Daddy" has long had this habit of pouring all my emotion into my work.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I always take time to study a planet before I apply the final brushstroke of Destruction to it.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Much like admiring the brushstrokes of an artwork, I too experience life alongside the living beings of a planet. Then, I slowly visualize how I would paint that world into my vision of hell.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I must admit, in Ahatopia, I subconsciously did a few... unnecessary things... Well, more than a few.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: It looks like these monsters are interfering with the sacred tree's root network...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Defeating them will hopefully help Evanescia a little.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: But it's exactly this extra bit of effort that allowed me to create {RUBY_B#Graphia, Himeko, and you}masterpieces I never dreamed of{RUBY_E#}. Watching you struggle, grow, and never give up hope... it gave me unparalleled joy.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Heh...just "masterpieces," huh. I see.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Thank you, Mr. Asat Pramad.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Thank you for placing me on the path of the Trailblaze. Thank you for acting for so long, and thank you for the adventure stories at bedtime...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: As "Ryusuke," you introduced me to stargazing, and so I learned to look up. You told me the Astral Express was real, igniting my obsession with finding it.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You sowed a false seed, but I nurtured it in my heart, and it sprouted into a desire for Trailblazing. The path you paved with lies is true to my companions and me. It has brought us here, and now...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I will stop you, and shatter your meticulously woven "Elation."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Hahahaha! Interesting! So very interesting!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Navigator, you never fail to surprise me! How quickly you dusted yourself off! How quickly you spring into a counterattack! "Patricide," they say, is the first step of growth. What will you do next? I look forward to it.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Patricide? On whom, my father, or the monster in front of me wearing his face as a mask? All I will do is rip off that mask.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I believe my true father's spirit is up there right now, watching on with delight...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And this grand entrance... Isn't it a bit much if all you came to do is watch me grow? Why are you really here? To join the Phantasmoon Games?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Bingo! I can feel it... the tides of panicked Wishpower impatient to swarm me!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: But the eight masks already have their owners. How exactly are you...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I'm sure everyone watching is as confused as "Miss Himeko" here. The eight Supplicants have already been determined. How would an unsought guest like me find a place in this Aeonic ceremony?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Ding-Dong! Recall! At the beginning of our story, our Lady Referee got a bit "creative" with the rules, and drew a mask for the "Protagonist."
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Oh?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: So, the rightful Mask of Elation, the one discarded for a fake... Whose hands did it fall into?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: The answer is right in front of you!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Planarcadia... What did you do!?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Prosperity breeds corruption, and suffering forges heroes. They revel in the moment, carefree, as if it were the night before arcadia was set to be destroyed.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Since they believe so fervently, then they deserve nothing less than this fate... to become flecks of crimson ink upon this apocalyptic landscape of the Demon Capital.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: ...Lunatic.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Destruction is more attractive to morbid curiosity than creation is.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But the artwork will not disappear. Even if it is defaced or lacerated, it will always live on as long as there is someone to remember it. It will be real as others recreate it over and over again.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Pity none of you will get the time to repaint it.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: B—Breaking news! We are hearing of an unprecedented major incident in Planarcadia!
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: Just moments ago, a new Supplicant announced they're joining the Phantasmoon Games!
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: I will lock you inside another painting, place you at the start of the lie that is Trailblazing, and you will be helpless.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: This Supplicant claims to be: Asat Pramad, a Lord Ravager serving under Nanook, the Aeon of Destruction!
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: According to eyewitness accounts, an entity suspected to be Asat Pramad appeared simultaneously in multiple locations, including Gothum City and Vehicle City, instantly causing massive destruction, for unknown reasons!
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: Is he just gonna ignore the eight-player rule!? Will the Department of Aberration Defense approve his participation? Speaking of which, what exactly has the Department of Aberration Defense been defending!?
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: Back-end data shows the online buzz surrounding tags like #AsatPramad and #LordRavager is intensifying! This also means Asat Pramad will gain a massive amount of Wishpower...
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: So... the Supplicant that ultimately wins the Phantasmoon Games and takes over as the Aeon of Elation... could be a Lord Ravager!
rows.speaker: Snowie

rows.text: We will continue to follow this story. We urge our viewers with any leads on Asat Pramad's whereabouts to contact us immediately!
rows.speaker: Poofy

rows.text: Okay... Did the teleporter spit us out in the wrong place?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: How long were we even gone? Is this place still the same Planarcadia as before...?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: There's no mistake. This is reality. The real Ahatopia.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: ...Where's Himeko?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It's not just the comms. Planarcadia's coordinate data is all over the place too. Where's Pearluxe Tower!?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: This space...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: (Call out Himeko's name)
Himeko! Can you hear me!?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Your anxious cries echo through the ruins, met with nothing but silence. From somewhere in the distance comes the rumble of collapsing debris... a cruel mockery of your desperate calls.
(Contact Himeko)
Static crackles through the phone. Nothing but white noise and a dead tone. The ominous interference sets your nerves on edge.
(Contact Express companions)
Static crackles through the phone. Nothing but white noise and a dead tone. The ominous interference sets your nerves on edge.
...It doesn't follow the laws of physics at all.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: It looks exactly like a thousand years ago, when the Legion tore the sky open. Asat Pramad finally got tired of just watching...
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: The opportunity he's been waiting for has finally arrived. The World in Canvas... no point in trapping the Voracity husk anymore.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: If Asat Pramad is so powerful, couldn't he just destroy this place and be done? Why bother joining the Phantasmoon Games?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: So, there's a further condition required to truly awaken it, that dead yet indestructible husk, slumbering for countless ages.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: A massive amount of Wishpower "activates" the husk... As it happens, the winner of the Games will be the Supplicant with the highest accumulated Wishpower!
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Exploiting the game's rules to win Aha's power, only to serve as the final offering to feed the Voracity?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Accumulating immense Wishpower...
Asat Pramad himself wants to serve up the Phantasmoon Games to the Voracity on a plate.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Ugh, just thinking about how "winner takes all" is meant literally in the Games, gives me the chills.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Would Aha really just sit back and let all this happen?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Aha's thoughts on this are one thing... but what the gods won't do, humanity must.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Just like before, we must stop Asat Pramad and rally all the power we can.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: The God of Games won't allow the rules to be broken.
We Nameless will do everything in our power.
The Nameless would never just stand idly by.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Cool, count me in. Either way, I don't want my game ending to be me in the belly of a leviathan.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: ...And I just got out of that maw. I don't intend to go back in any time soon.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Let me try. Initiating all-channel scan.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Bad news, [Trailblazer]. The whole academy is dark... In other words, besides us, there isn't a single living soul here.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I know we've got important things to deal with right now...
Not one person?
And Himeko... Hope she's alright.
Where are the students? The teachers...?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Don't be so negative. Maybe your boss lady evacuated them.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: It's too early to jump to conclusions.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Even if her opponent is a Lord Ravager, she'll definitely hold her own.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Let us walk a bit farther ahead. The answer might be there.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Himeko! Where are you!?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: There is a scent of the Abundance... What are those veins of light stretching out from the Phantasmoon?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Are those... the roots of the sacred tree?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: ...Evanescia?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: This fissure... sure looks like the mouth of the Voracity.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Little Raccoon...
Come... here...
Is that Evanescia's voice...?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Little Raccoon... I knew you'd find me. Just like you...found her...
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: Graphia, it's been a while.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: Evanescia... I've painted you countless times, for thousands of years... but nothing compares to seeing you here, in this moment.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: It's truly wonderful seeing you again... and it's thanks to [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: I heard you're looking for {RUBY_B#Himeko}Himekat{RUBY_E#}, yes?
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: Is she okay!?
I can't pinpoint her exact location, but I can still sense her life force. She is likely doing fine...
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: ...That's good.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You don't look too good.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Now this is a first, the sacred tree of Abundance, so withered...
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Maintaining a shattered reality always comes at a cost. I had to temporarily... borrow this painting to materialize.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: I know you, and the little one behind you... Hehehe! So the Baseball Raccoon's frenemies, the Star Catchers, have shown up too.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: What exactly happened here?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Asat Pramad completed his "roll-call" and made the "miracle" happen. He brought the end of the world.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: And are you going to do something about it, being an arbitrator?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: My apologies, I have more pressing matters to attend to at present...
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: The end is here, and the lands are disintegrating and shattering. I have to... hold tightly to its remains. I must fulfill my duty as the Panarch Elwood, I must preserve the life of this world.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: How tragic... as if the world was back in that age when all things were reduced to cinders.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: I'm sorry, Evanescia. I couldn't protect the World in Canvas.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: No, you did it, Graphia. You hid the world inside the painting. You left behind a glimmer of hope.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: Time powers? How is that even fair?
A thousand years later, and the hope we've been waiting for has finally arrived. New Nameless and those willing to save this world have returned once again.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: We don't have long. It's a race against time to stop Asat Pramad.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: What I sense of Asat Pramad's apocalypse is... impermanence, like an unstable future.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: But if no one stops it, then it will become real.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: Evanescia!
Are you saying that meanie has the power to manipulate "time"...?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: No wonder my attacks missed every single time we fought... that cheating jerk!
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: We still have a sliver of opportunity before the dust settles.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: The die is still in the air, we still have... a chance to snatch it, roll a different number, and shape the future into... something else.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: Ngh...
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: Evanescia...
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Ah... it seems I am still not so great at multitasking...
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: I won't let Evanescia down.
But I know the final page of the story hasn't been turned yet.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: Little Raccoon, I can sense it... Your Express friends are unharmed. They're just... scattered all over.
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: Follow the roots of the Arbor, find Himekat, find your companions. I know...
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: You always have something up your sleeve, don't you, Protagonist?
rows.speaker: Evanescia

rows.text: She's gone.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: What a shame... Reunited after a thousand years, and we can't even catch up properly.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: The clock is ticking. Let's get moving.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'll find Himeko, locate the rest of the crew, and teach Asat Pramad a lesson!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Let's follow those faint threads of golden light.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: They're an extension of Evanescia's life force, and the beacon she was able to leave us.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Following it will take us exactly where we need to go.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Didn't you say there wouldn't be any other signs of life?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Do these things even count as lifeforms?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Evanescia's roots are guiding us... Where are we?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What's off about this painting?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I... want to find Himeko.
Someone might've left something on it.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Huh? What's this?
Himeko!
Bladie...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Is this the Navigator you've been looking for?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: She left a single stroke on the canvas, a record of the final moments of her standoff with Asat Pramad. She was very brave.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Thank you, Blade.
She is your descendant...
...and the greatest Navigator!
She is your descendant, and for me, the most amazing Express Navigator.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: My... descendant? You're saying... one of my descendants became the Navigator of the Astral Express?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Thank you for telling me this. I feel like a thousand years of waiting... has finally been rewarded.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Do you still want to keep testing me, Asat Pramad?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Since the Express's return to Planarcadia, you've been constantly picking at me over what happened fifteen years ago.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You've had countless chances to kill me all this time, but you didn't show your true colors until I exposed you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Asat Pramad, what exactly are you wary of?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You could always see it as fatherly concern...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Do Lord Ravagers even have human emotions?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Why not? I can feel curious, enraged... I understand humans — the very targets of our Destruction — better than my colleagues. I even get herniated discs and tendinitis...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Aren't you a Lord Ravager?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I will lock you inside another painting, place you at the start of the lie that is Trailblazing, and you will be helpless.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Does the power of the Destruction include the ability to cure tendinitis?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Now, as I was saying, child, you are absolutely right that I am full of curiosity about you...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: What exactly happened to you and Himeko that night fifteen years ago?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You were surprised too, weren't you? Your dicey head probably exploded with questions the moment that iron giant Pegana's Legacy appeared.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What is she talking about?
"You and Himeko"?
"Pegana's Legacy"?
Your curiosity can't stand the existence of questions. If you don't solve them, the unknown becomes an obstacle to your plans, and wipes the smile off your face.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Oh?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You say you understand humans, Asat Pramad, but you do not. At all. I didn't run away that night... We didn't run.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: My companions on the Express, the friends I respect, wouldn't run either.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Even if the Navigator weren't around, they would still ignite the Express's engines and win the Phantasmoon Games.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Is Himeko hinting something at me?
"Ignite the Express's engines"...?
Win the Phantasmoon Games?
("Ignite the Express's engines and win the Phantasmoon Games." ...Are these clues Himeko left for us?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Himeko must have had a reason for saying that. I need to calm down... I can't let her down.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You will learn of the secret from fifteen years ago soon enough. But, you must submit to my interrogation too. Asat Pramad, do you accept this challenge?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You've extended such an open invitation. Wouldn't it be rude of me to refuse?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Those who shrink from a challenge do not deserve the reward. A fine tenet for those who follow the path of Elation.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Both for you, and for me...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You've been watching us for quite a while now. Dear audience, have you been enjoying our little show?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Himeko!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Surely you are not about to cry...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: How exquisitely touching!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: The forbear of artists graces the academy that bears her name. Forgive me for not greeting you sooner, in my capacity as the dean.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: It surprises me that you have not been consumed by madness.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You must be disappointed... Asat Pramad.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Just the opposite, I am quite satisfied.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Before my clones pick you off one by one, I'd like to play the spectator too, and see you in action.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Where did you take Himeko!?
Where did you take Himeko!?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Where did I "take" her? She challenged me, and I gladly accepted. Nothing more.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: [Trailblazer], be sure you don't fail the request she left behind.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: This is also my challenge to you.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I hope you enjoy the apocalypse.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Meanie dice! We're not done here!
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: You've shown us your tricks, but you haven't seen mine.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: The time of the sword has arrived.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: {RUBY_B#This body}The tempered sword{RUBY_E#} now thirsts for blood to sharpen its blade.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: You won't be playing alone, Silver Wolf.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Hahahahaha!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: That's right, yes! Finally the game gets interesting!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: He's gone... Cowardly rat.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Is it just my imagination, or was *this* Asat Pramad way less sneaky than the one we faced in the World in Canvas?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Do you mean that might not have been Asat Pramad...?
He didn't even want to come near us.
That clone's aura felt quite genuine.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Asat Pramad isn't the type of opponent to shy away from a fight.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Bladie?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: My player intuition says the reason that meanie dice is avoiding us has something to do with the truth about his abilities... It's like Evanescia said. He can pull off some kind of trick that messes with time.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Uncovering the truth about his abilities might just be the way we end this apocalypse. But who has time to figure that out right now!
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I'd die before agreeing with the IPC... but Pearl is right. Escorting Graphia to Pearluxe Tower is the most logical choice right now.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: What do you say, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Y—Yeah, okay, right now the most important thing is to finish Himeko's task.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: But I'm still really worried about her, and about losing contact with Dan Heng and Welt.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I will go to that abandoned station and find them.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Don't worry about me, Silver Wolf.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: No, I just wanted to say something before you go: It's good to have you back.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Thank you, Bladie. I need to stop letting my imagination get the better of me.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It's time I did what I need to do: carry out Himeko's wishes.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Stay calm. First, I need to find the Express and ignite the engine)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (The whole world has changed. How do I find Perdido Station now?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Help! Don't come any closer!
rows.speaker: Calling Civilian

rows.text: What on earth is happening here...
rows.speaker: Calling Civilian

rows.text: Gimme your... Wishpower! Devour! Consume!
rows.speaker: Out-of-Control Imagenae

rows.text: Seems I might need to go over there and help.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Have these guys gone mad?
rows.speaker: Calling Civilian

rows.text: Run for your lives!
rows.speaker: Calling Civilian

rows.text: Looks like we'll catch up with Sunday's birds pretty soon...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Let's keep pressing ahead.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: My store, my house, all gone! Standing one second, reduced to ashes the next!
rows.speaker: Rescued Citizen

rows.text: Stay strong!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Guys look! It's th-the Lord Ravager's apocalyptic livestream!
rows.speaker: Rescued Citizen

rows.text: Did you catch that hero saving people just now? Quick, check if it's hit 100K likes yet!
rows.speaker: Rescued Citizen

rows.text: Still filming!? Those shots are not worth dying for!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Thank you! Thank you!
rows.speaker: Rescued Citizen

rows.text: Quickly! Go find shelter in Perdido Station!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Everyone, behind me!
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: ...It's Cinderborne.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Do not fear! Get behind me! Cinderborne... never backs down!
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: That sounded like... is that Thundercoil? Thundercoil went mad too!?
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: Keep going, charge straight ahead!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Watch out, don't get hit!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's the Daybreak Warrior! He's going to cast his ultimate!
rows.speaker: Naive Child

rows.text: Hey, kid? That's just a show, okay? Make believe! Look around you, we're all going to die here!
rows.speaker: Desperate Citizen

rows.text: Just get behind me!
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: Senior...!? It's you! Th-This is awesome!
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: Don't worry, I'm here!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Yoohoo, Gray Hair! Need a little outside support from the tavern?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Oh? Magnus is here too? How are you doing there, kid?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Mr. Ashveil? I'm fine! Just relieved to have my senior and everyone else here!
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: We'd just finished handling an issue at the tavern, only to walk right into this crazy commotion.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Gray Hair, you've had Planarcadia's top streamer waiting on you hand and foot for so long. How about you keep your promise? Where's my mask?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Sure, sure. But... I was hoping you could help me with one more little thing.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I figured you'd start bargaining. Since when did our deal include this many add-ons?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Of course, saving people is great and all. But first, we've got to get rid of that thing.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Hehe, come on... play with me!
rows.speaker: "Reflection of the Demonic Moon"

rows.text: We meet again, Cinderborne!
Hehe, forever... forever together!
rows.speaker: "Reflection of the Demonic Moon"

rows.text: So that purple lightbulb thing is what made those imagenae snap?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Exactly... Those pulses it's sending out are driving people into panic. If we don't take it down, anyone we help will just fall under its influence again.
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: Argh!
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: It felt like something was drilling into my head just now...
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: You'd think seeing the sky being torn open during the apocalypse would be much more panic-inducing...
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Hey, snap out of it! We're talking about real danger here...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Alright, buckle up, buttercups! This giant device here is a mega panic signal transmitter. The more you freak out, the stronger it gets! If you let it scare you, you've already lost, capiche?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: I see... you're not here to play with me at all!
rows.speaker: "Reflection of the Demonic Moon"

rows.text: Nasty, nasty people!
rows.speaker: "Reflection of the Demonic Moon"

rows.text: The moon has nearly landed...
rows.speaker: Terrified Civilian

rows.text: There will be no more sorrow, no more pain...
rows.speaker: Disoriented Civilian

rows.text: [Trailblazer], when these people saw you, they felt the joy of survival.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: And that joy... that's true proof of being alive.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: These people should thank me for bringing them true elation.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: C'mere, [Trailblazer], let's play!!!
rows.speaker: "Reflection of the Demonic Moon"

rows.text: So, how did the tavern investigation go?
Seeing as you honored your promise and returned the mask, Gray Hair, I'll help you out one last time.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Now!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Hoo...! Groo... Groooo!
rows.speaker: "Reflection of the Demonic Moon"

rows.text: Sparxie...burned a Lord Ravager...
H—Help...! Help meee...! I'm scared of the dark...
rows.speaker: "Reflection of the Demonic Moon"

rows.text: That monstrous moon is gone...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Heh, all that laughter, now just look how miserable you are.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: So the imagenae spreading panic is actually a coward too. How pathetic.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Haha, why does this kind of feel like picking on a little kid...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I... I just now... what happened to me?
rows.speaker: Stupefied Lightpaw

rows.text: Did... I do all this?
rows.speaker: Reactivated Mechatron

rows.text: You did it, senior [Trailblazer]! Everyone has regained their senses!
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: Mr. Ashveil...
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: Nicely done, Magnus. With the world crumbling around them, it must mean a lot for kids to see their hero step in and save the day.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Thank you, Mr. Ashveil. But could we change the subject...? It's kind of embarrassing.
rows.speaker: Cinderborne

rows.text: No idea where Mister N is right now... I wonder if he's safe...
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I beg you.
Oh? What is this, Gray Hair? Coming off your noble high horse to save lives? This beats even reaching ten million followers!
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Is there a better way to get even more followers?
Totally! Being known as the savior of Planarcadia!? That's a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's right, we were ambushed by an individual claiming to be Asat Pramad.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Fortunately, the chivalrous Sparxicle generously came to our aid. I then proposed an idea: between us, we exploited our knowledge of the tavern's complex layout to corner him into a room of our choosing, locked it, then...
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: We tossed that room and Asat Pramad into the star of Sedounirama, and burned him to ashes.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Don't doubt it. It's even more authentic than Pearl. But...
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Compared to what we should expect from a Lord Ravager, our fellow was more like an illusion, rather, a counterfeit double used to divert attention.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Silver Wolf and I also encountered Asat Pramad. Even Himeko, she encountered him at the academy...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What!? So Himeko...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't worry. Himeko has a plan. She wants us to start up the Express and gather everyone.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: The path to Perdido Station should be clear now. Well then, Sparxicle will be on her way.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: You're not coming with us?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: All that neat, coordinated action? Not Sparxicle's style, I'm more a one-girl show.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: I'd like for you to open the tavern doors, so that civilians with nowhere to go at least have a place to stay.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Ugh, Gray Hair, you really love putting people on the spot. So what, we repurpose the World's End Tavern into some kind of bunker?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: That place isn't open to just anyone. Besides... given the situation, even hiding there might not be safe.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: While the Fools do find joy in chaos, I doubt such utter, sweeping destruction is the sort of amusement your kind wants to see.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: For the older generation of Fools, yes, but we're in a different time. Most young Masked Fools would lock those tavern doors tightly. So Gray Hair, you really need my help?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Hmm... fine, I suppose I can spare a little kindness.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: I need to first take these Sparxheads to the tavern~ Then, Gray Hair, I might think about your proposal.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Thanks to you, Sunny, we at least have a safe place in these apocalyptic times!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: "That is my duty. Admittedly, present circumstances are far more... dangerous than I anticipated."
rows.speaker: Crow

rows.text: We're moving as fast as we can.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: "I have never had cause to doubt your resolve. Trouble is, the road ahead is far more... dangerous than I had anticipated."
rows.speaker: Crow

rows.text: Just look! This isn't the old Sparxie anymore. At this rate, I might even be able to compete with you for the title in the Phantasmoon Games.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Sneaky! You're stealing followers!
Don't you think you're exaggerating a bit!?
I accept your challenge!
Hmph! Do you think we would be watching your highlights now, if it wasn't for Sparxie's support?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Just kidding, Did the Voracity steal your sense of humor or what?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: That's the spirit. Let's see who saves the most people, okay?
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: You're trying to manipulate me!
Oh-ho, humans always use anger to mask their fear.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: With Sparxie's mask on, they've basically earned a ticket into the Tavern.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Don't worry, while Sparxicle is here, no Sparxhead that loves me is getting left behind.
rows.speaker: Sparxie

rows.text: Quick, look over there! Sunday's bird!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Sunday, can you hear me!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "Miss March?"
rows.speaker: Crow

rows.text: Finally, we've been waiting forever to get a hold of you!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "The imagenae at Perdido Station were restless, but just now they suddenly calmed down. I figured you must have done something."
rows.speaker: Crow

rows.text: "My tuning services are no longer required for the restoration of sanity. I can now fully focus on guiding the birds your way."
rows.speaker: Crow

rows.text: Danger's been a constant companion on this path.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: It's not that much further to Perdido Station! Come on, let's go meet up with Sunday!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Planarcadia is scrambled, just like a puzzle cube... nothing's where it should be...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Your poor Navigator believes you can turn the tide, defeat me, and keep the star rail moving forward.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I wonder, [Trailblazer], CAN you do all that?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I might as well reveal a secret to you, as a reward of sorts.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: The Navigator you place so much faith in, is nothing more than a thief assuming the identity of "Himeko", an imagenae that steals fates, an impostor.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Enough of your delusions! Lies or not, you won't weaken my resolve!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It was Himeko who led us to the Express, and she's been with us every step of the way. You think you can shake us with her past, but that means nothing to us!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Fascinating, trust built on willful ignorance of the truth. I eagerly await your next move!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Watch out, they're here!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Careful, blindly charging in will get you fried to a crisp.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: [Trailblazer], you need to pay attention to the pattern of the lightning strikes.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: All this thunder and lighting is making my poor ears ring!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Phew... just having a ceiling over my head makes me feel much safer.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Excellent, you're here at last!
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Excellent, you're finally here.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What happened to the Astral Express?
Apologies, after the disaster struck, falling rubble blocked the route to the platform.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: At the time, I was tending to the wounded in the hall. By the time I realized I should start the train, it was already too late.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Pom-Pom...
Having heeded the whispers of Yao Guang, the bird flapped its wings and soared deeper into the ruins...
Don't blame yourself.
I'm trying my utmost to reestablish communication with the conductor.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Don't be too hard on yourself, Mr. Sunday! The Astral Express isn't going to fall apart that easily. If it were me, I'd have chosen to save people first too.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The collapsed passageway buried the Express. Well then, we'll just dig it out!
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Thank you, I'm fine. The sight of the Demon Capital unsettled me. Shall we resume planning our next course of action?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'll go check the damage to the passageway. We'll need the Express if we're going to fight Asat Pramad.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Mr. Ashveil, before that, a... monkey gentleman arrived here with refugees from Dovebrook District... Perhaps you know him?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...Mister N!? I knew he'd be smart enough to survive.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Everyone, excuse me for a little while, I need to check in with an old friend.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: [Trailblazer], if you have the time, please speak with the people stuck here.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: While tuning can ease their inner emotional turmoil, it cannot blind them to the calamity in front of them.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The fear within them must be illuminated by hope. And right now, you, the one who once triumphed over Fulwish and saved them, are the most fitting choice.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Dan Heng and Mr. Yang aren't back yet... We should go find General Yao Guang and ask her what's going on.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: General, are Dan Heng and Mr. Yang alright?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm sorry. Asat Pramad attacked the moment we finished setting up the formations, dragging us into an endless fight. Mr. Yang stepped in and sent me away from the battlefield to help the Express instead.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Dan Heng... Mr. Yang... I'm really worried about them.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Before leaving, I placed talismans on them for good fortune. Based on what I can sense right now, the two of them should be safe.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I'm worried about them too.
With their skills and a little luck, I'm sure they'll be safe.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: In times like these, we have to believe in our companions. As for us, we need to focus on the matter at hand.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Blade went to the abandoned station to help them.
Whether friend or foe, Stellaron Hunters are powerful. Since they are the former right now, I would rather focus on our current situation.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: "Azure One, Vermilion Five, aligned Sky, come forth." Help me find that Hunter.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I'll try sharing the location of the talisman with Blade. Hopefully, the message will reach him safely.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: The unbreakable March will pull herself together too! I'll go check on the buried Express.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer], we'll be counting on you to reassure everyone!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Mommy didn't make it out...
rows.speaker: Melancholic Survivor

rows.text: Will somebody come and help us!
rows.speaker: Helpless Survivor

rows.text: "Warning: Power levels critical. Non-combat modules have been deactivated."
rows.speaker: IPC Security Mechatron

rows.text: It's dying too? We're done for, game over!
rows.speaker: Despairing Survivor

rows.text: I was trapped on the street, then a talking monkey saved me!
rows.speaker: Bewildered Survivor

rows.text: Is it possible you hit your head on something?
rows.speaker: Clear-Headed Survivor

rows.text: I thought you had a few more bright ideas.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But in the end, your only idea is to leave me "trapped in the canvas?"
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I know what you are plotting.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: We don't know each other well, and we both long for truth. Perhaps you feel you hide your secrets well.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: But this does not exist in my imagenated world.
This room...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Since it's a challenge, it must have a theme. I have thought of one for you.
This "artwork" is for you, its theme is the past of a father and daughter.
...Made in the same way you turned a city into ruins?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Correct, but alas, like the iron giant you summoned, this piece is still far from completion.
And that is why I've invited you to join me in completing this artwork I have named "Himeko."
As her dear father, I know the first half of her life. But there are three blanks, corresponding to three secrets, hidden in your memories.
So a "quiz" but in a different format.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Of course, but only in the interest of fairness. That way, when we finish the artwork, both of us have an equal chance of having our secrets revealed.
The first to uncover their opponent's trump card takes the victory.
I accept.
I refuse.
You expect me to just play by your rules? I wouldn't hold my breath.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Child, you relinquished the right to refuse when you decided to challenge me.
So, let's start.
Himeko, your old man is back!
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: And with a present you will love!
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Friendly reminder: you may only speak to "Ryusuke" right now.
Will you not even talk to your father!?
Remember this day? It was your birthday.
You asked me where the center of the universe was. Well, your old man racked his brains over and over, and found the answer.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: This is a ceramic comet ship model, have it.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: I don't quite know where the center of the universe is. But you can pilot this ship and find out yourself, when you're older.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Because the universe does have an end. And at that end is a tiny dot of light that people run to once they spot it, and upsies they go!
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: And one day, it will be you, Himeko, flying up to the stars too!
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: (Don't let his words hypnotize you.)
Why are you impersonating Ryusuke?
What the heck do you want?
You are trying to keep your mind blank, but that is futile. Wishpower is far more responsive than memoria. It appears faster than you can think.
"That means Daddy has been to the end of the universe?"
rows.speaker: Voice in the Memory

rows.text: Unfortunately, no. Only to the end of the world.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: But I know that the end of the universe is called Pegana, even though I haven't been there myself...
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: But your old man does know someone from there.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: The someone who's been to Pegana... Is it Akivili?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...That's ancient history.
Now that I think about it, you always intentionally left "little openings" during my childhood.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Was this also part of your scheme?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: As I said, my only lie to Himeko is the lie that I am Ryusuke.
If some things said on occasion are incongruous to the character, that is entirely unintentional.
For example, I felt a bit emotional seeing the comet ships lying among the ruins of Delkor Ring that I had just destroyed.
You really are a monster.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko of the past didn't think so. Shall we continue the fun?
Took a bit of time off from all that routine civilization destroying work. Isn't it so much more interesting to live there for a spell, and watch a world you know so well fall into ruin?
Enough questions! Let's return to our warm and fuzzy trip down memory lane.
Cut! Old Himeko would never say such things.
Come on, throw me a bone here, I can't do this show alone.
But your old man does know someone from there.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: This line bothers me.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Do you know the Trailblaze Aeon?
What kind of world was Pegana?
Do you have any insider information about the Astral Express?
Is Akivili really dead?
Good question, you must be desperate for the answer.
Of course, I will not be giving it to you.
But your old man does know someone from there.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: From there! From there! From there!
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: It appears you will find no more clues here.
Did you laugh?
What are you painting there, Himeko?
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Hm, it's not a Bullet Wyrm. It must be a train... a flying train! Have you been peeking into my manuscript?
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: ...Your old man is not angry at all. How could I be? I'm so happy that you are quite the little explorer!
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: But why not just ask? Come, your old man will tell you the story of the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Tell the story of the Astral Express.
Tell the story of the Lord Ravager.
Tell the story of Ryusuke.
Do you enjoy role-playing?
Now, we move to the legend of "a certain Navigator." It's my favorite story.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: It is said that after the fall of the Trailblaze Aeon, THEIR followers left one after another. And by the end, there was only one Navigator and one Nameless left in the once-massive crew.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: One day, a History Fictionologist snuck aboard the Express and tampered with the navigation log. But the next day, the logbook was completely unchanged.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: And a cloaked Navigator was sitting there, bored to death, flipping through the records.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: "How on earth?" asked the History Fictionologist.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: "Because I remember each and every one of their names," said the Navigator, "along with the coordinates of every star, and the trajectory of every meteor."
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Certainly! But you can only get the answers you seek if you pick the first option.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Pause. Here Ryusuke is getting ready to head to the planet Goliath's Shepherd. To destroy it.
He probably can't just tell Himeko: "You be good, Daddy is off to do some murdering."
Of course. Should I not?
You never hesitate to mention the Astral Express. In fact, you don't stop talking about it.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Was it necessary to role-play my father to this extent?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's a terrible habit of mine.
It wouldn't be the habit of Navigator "Isee," would it?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You figured that out already? Well that's boring.
The way you spoke about that {RUBY_B#Pegana's Legacy}mechatron{RUBY_E#} was enough to know... {RUBY_B#Isee}He{RUBY_E#} is your other mask.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Fair enough. And you did send people to sniff around the tavern for answers. It was only a matter of time before you figured it out.
But I swear, all I wanted at first was to be a loving father.
Himeko's Weathering Curse worsened this year. I couldn't help myself, I gave her a beautiful dream. And in return... hahaha! Fortune makes fools of us all.
Fortune makes fools of us all... The Masked Fool "Enroute," Navigator "Isee"... They are all our enemy "Asat Pramad" in the end.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Congratulations! Kindly accept this reward. It is your ticket to the truth.
Open that door.
"Because I remember each and every one of their names. Along with the coordinates of every star, and the trajectory of every meteor."
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: There's actually a second part.
They were all reduced to a deathly silence.
I remember something... Behind this door...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...is where the first secret is buried.
Other than her "self-portrait," no one knows the story of how Himeko found and repaired the stranded Express.
It's your turn to choose. To move on, or to stop? Is there really a choice for a Navigator?
Unlock the sealed past.
Just ignore him.
You will stay right here? Sure. I have plenty of time. Do you?
In this place... ah, I have never been here as your father!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Look at it! We can work very happily together here, can't we?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: So, she built herself a secret base while "Ryusuke" was away?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: My mother's studio remained empty since her passing. I took the opportunity to use it.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Sounds convincing.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: A bar, too. Do minors drink here?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: She was already in college by then.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Shall we have a drink? I learned from Bragi, Phantylia couldn't stop raving about my mixing.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: ...No, thank you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: By the time she finds the Express, the Weathering Curse would've consumed her.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Himeko is always in such a tough spot, isn't she?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I guess you don't know.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That day was your "daughter's" birthday.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Ah. Fortune makes fools of us all.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Her loneliest birthday ever. To her, even death was less terrifying than not having her family, than them disappearing without a trace, as if they had never existed.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: She ran from home to chase stars, but lost her way and could only wander in the dark.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Water swirling around her ankles, weeds slashing her skin. And then...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: She saw it, there on the shores of the "World in Canvas."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: There are many ways to reach the sky.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: She chose the most unrealistic one and wasted the rest of her life.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You're wrong. That night, the stars gave her the best gift.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In this vast universe, nothing holds more beauty than "the lands en route, yet to be reached."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But they can be reached, with the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: These blueprints tell me that the Express is not the only thing she is researching.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Pegana's Legacy. I have always thought this legend disappeared along with Akivili.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: But it seems there has been some meddling.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Are you afraid of the Starblazer?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Starblazer... A name of Himeko's own invention? Her sense of humor is even worse than {RUBY_B#former navigator}Dolly{RUBY_E#}'s.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: In ancient times, these humanoid weapons helped Pegana conquer countless planets. They invaded, destroyed, then glorified as "the Trailblaze."
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: But in the images shown to me by the Express, these "giants" joined hands with the Express crew.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The hand holding a tool defines what that tool becomes. In one hand, the scepter triggers a brutal war. In another's hand, the scepter creates new worlds.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I thought this too. Before my head turned into a die.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: But then Akivili died. The Omen Vanguards began spreading the murmurs of Terminus, and not even Nous could stop the birth of the Destruction.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: THEY all failed.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Yet, you are different? I shall wait and see.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: The giant reaching for the stars, the myth of Pegana...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: She performed a miracle in this world of no imagination.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: As to how it was created, dear old pal Akivili never spoke a word.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: But my daughter replicated the blueprint purely from guesswork. My daughter really is a genius, isn't she?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Would you like to know the secret?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: No. My dice head wouldn't be able to make heads or tails of such technical details.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: What must a girl, powerless but longing for the sky think, to see a giant walking among the stars?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: She can only draw that dream.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: "I want to be as free and powerful as they are."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: So, that isn't a reforged weapon, but a manifestation of Himeko herself?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: That explains why it is incomplete. Himeko is already dead.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Don't waste your energy. I've seen all your tricks on this journey.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: But an incomplete imagenae cannot break this world.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You're right. And neither can it be broken by you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Because you know nothing about what follows, and you have no way to imagenate it.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: How did I start the Express? What miracles did I witness at the end of the Phantasmoon Games? You must allow me to take over if you want to continue on.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We all know you have no other choice.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...Of course, this painting can be altered for you, if you so wish.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: It is, after all, the way "you" were born, yes?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Please, let us proceed to the next part of Himeko's life.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Himeko was lucky. She found the stranded Express and began to repair it.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Unfortunately, her condition deteriorated rapidly shortly after.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: She was in and out of the sanatorium, but the clock kept ticking down.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Her stamina worsened by the day. Simply returning to the Express was hard enough, what more reaching the stars?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: She was eventually left with a single choice.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Your turn to create. Open that window, and fill in the second blank...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: "Your" history with Himeko will also be recreated in this painting.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I can't wait to see how it turns out.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Do you know how many times you've failed to escape?
rows.speaker: Nurse

rows.text: Do you remember how many paintings you produced in class?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: You know your condition. Take your medicine on time, avoid strenuous exercise.
rows.speaker: Nurse

rows.text: And lie down more often. I'm a Graphia Academy graduate too, I know what it takes to paint.
rows.speaker: Nurse

rows.text: You can keep me here, that's fine. But do you also have to meddle with my creative exploits?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Keep being like this. See if I'll help you next time the doctors catch you.
rows.speaker: Nurse

rows.text: This painting is so beautiful... Is it your sister? But I remember...
rows.speaker: Nurse

rows.text: No, it's my self-portrait.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: A self I can never become...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: As long as you're still willing to paint and imagine a better version of yourself, then there's still hope.
rows.speaker: Nurse

rows.text: I'll be going now. Remember to pick Wednesday for your next escape attempt. I won't be on duty that day.
rows.speaker: Nurse

rows.text: I'm back...
rows.speaker: ???&Motoko

rows.text: Still giving the nurse a hard time?
Are you going to lecture me too?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Of course not. Why that face? Did something good happen?
Oh, it's nothing.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Looking at this painting reminds me of the day we met...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: A little wiser and more optimistic, a little prettier.
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: Add some color here.
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: And also... Hm, let's see what the Navigators in the logbook are like...
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: Someone with the courage to fight for what's right, even if they can't gain the upper hand.
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: Someone who's always ready to go ahead, even when there are wheels within wheels.
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: Would be even better if she was more mature, like Dolly or Isee.
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: Sketch out the form using my own memories and the stories of the Nameless as a skeleton *cough*...
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: And finally, I inject her with Wishpower and materialize her by imagenesis!
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: What a fresh face!
rows.speaker: Self-Portrait

rows.text: Hello, Creator.
rows.speaker: Self-Portrait

rows.text: It worked! She's really alive!
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: Calm yourself, I am not going anywhere.
rows.speaker: Self-Portrait

rows.text: So, um... hello!? Oh right, sorry, I haven't given you a name yet!
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: Shouldn't we begin with introductions?
rows.speaker: Self-Portrait

rows.text: Himeko, Murata Himeko.
rows.speaker: Expectant Girl

rows.text: Nice to meet you, Himeko. As for me, you can call me...
rows.speaker: Self-Portrait

rows.text: Motoko. The repair work on the Express is proceeding smoothly, thanks to you.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: By the way, are the heating pipes fixed now?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: As you said, we just needed to change the conductors. Anyway, guess what I brought you?
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: This is the Express's blueprint...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I've also brought drawing tools, an imaging device... everything I could think of.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Your symptoms are getting worse and worse, and you have less and less time to go home.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Knowing you, there's no way you'd stop worrying about the Express. You might be stuck in the sanatorium, but your heart's still at the workshop.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: So, I realized we could bring the workshop to you.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: At night, you can review these and tell me what to do. In the daytime, I'll be your hands and feet and help you repair it little by little.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Just like we always do.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Sorry for making you worry.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Don't worry about that, nothing wrong with failing.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Think of it this way: There will always be someone to repair the Astral Express, and not necessarily us. Either way, our hard work will be enough to help whoever that is.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: But I promised to bring the Express home. I want to deliver on that promise.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I know.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: So, remember I am here with you. Lean on me when you feel you can't hold on.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: I will remember.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I almost forgot! While I was waiting for you to come over, I came up with a never-before-seen coffee recipe. Want to give it a try?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Hopefully it's not canned alien angler fish.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: I'll go get some water first.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Miss, the Sanatorium is closed. Please come back tomorrow.
rows.speaker: Doctor

rows.text: As I recall, the doctors here only have night shifts on Wednesday.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Did you not say it was my turn to create?
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: I'm just participating in my own way.
rows.speaker: Doctor (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: With her condition worsening, Himeko can only think of one solution: imagenate a new version of herself.
rows.speaker: Doctor (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: A healthier, more mature version of herself she imagines would "become the Navigator."
rows.speaker: Doctor (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: In other words, you, Motoko.
rows.speaker: Doctor (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Are you done? I need to go to her.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Sure. I'll be expecting you back, to tell me more.
rows.speaker: Doctor (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: I'm just a doctor on his rounds. I didn't see or hear anything.
rows.speaker: Doctor (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Miss, are you mistaken?
rows.speaker: Door (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: The women's bathroom is on the other side.
rows.speaker: Door (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Please stop knocking, this is not the Golden Confessional.
rows.speaker: Door (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: No matter your pains and suffering, you may neither pour nor flush them away here.
rows.speaker: Door (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: I thought you were cosplaying that Golden Toilet.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: When it comes to character selection, even I have my limits.
rows.speaker: Door (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Himeko, are you stargazing?
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: I'm wondering how far we can go once the Express can depart.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: The farthest I see is a third-tier star, located ten thousand light-years away. But after that...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Past that distance, I will need to use my feet to measure the stars.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: We're running out of time.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Motoko, what's the success rate of igniting the engine?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: "...0.21 percent."
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: It's gone down but 1 percent...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: When I found the Express, it flew me up into the sky. And now, it will not move at all.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: After eliminating hundreds of malfunctions, replacing thousands of parts, here we are, stuck... In the end, it is an engine with zero dynamism.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Are you okay?
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: I'm... alright. It's just the engine. We can handle that.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I'll think, and you'll do. Just like usual.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: It's getting late. You should go get some rest. Even imagenae can't work day and night.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: We will do it, Himeko. We will reach the sky.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Sure.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: The engine...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Will I really be able to fix the Express?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: How far can someone who can barely walk get, even if they leave Ahatopia?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: The Weathering Curse would tear me apart when I cross the atmosphere.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I have the Astral Express, I know interstellar travel dynamics, the navigator's log is with me, and I have Motoko. Everything necessary to embark on this journey...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Except time.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I'm sorry, Motoko. Ten thousand light-years is too far.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: How touching. I could cry!
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Unfortunately, I don't have eyes to cry out of.
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: I've spent twenty years looking up at this hospital ceiling.
rows.speaker: Coughing Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: I heard that if you win the Games, you can make a wish to an Aeon. Even if that wish is just to see real stars...
rows.speaker: Excited Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Himeko, I have an idea.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: The moon is full. Let's enter the Phantasmoon Games together.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Pray to The Laughter, the almighty, to grant you a healthy...
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: There's no point, Motoko. Our ancestors already tried...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Some of them died on the eve of the Games, some were defeated in competition, and only one of them won: Murata Hiro.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: But unfortunately, he went missing. All he left was a note saying: "Elation" does not cure the curse.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Thank you, Motoko, but no one can fulfill my wish, not even the Aeons.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: We'll make a new wish then, not for you to live.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Then what for?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: To go out with a bang! To return the Express to the skies, and push it closer and closer to the stars.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Let's pray to The Laughter to ignite the engine! And make it so everyone sees the Astral Express set forth anew!
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Even if all THEY do is laugh, THEY can at least turn the Express into a firework and send it roaring and flashing into the sky!
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Then... what kind of "miracle" should we create? And what about my condition?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: How about we use the "Starblazer" blueprint you restored to create a giant robot?
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: They'll see. I'll be your hand and foot, and you will put an iron giant right in front of them all.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: I broke into your home safe and took this mask. You wouldn't make me come all this way for nothing, would you?
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: You're right, Motoko... If there is no cure for the Weathering Curse...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Then at the very least, we should put my final moments to use and create that "dream" together.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Hahaha... You're even more interesting than I thought. Others are always trying to steal from the gods. But all you want is a brilliant fireworks show.
rows.speaker: Projectionist (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: And of course, my sweet daughter actually accepted this ridiculous suggestion.
rows.speaker: Projectionist (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Touching, truly! And what did she have to give up to enter the Phantasmoon Games fifteen years ago?
rows.speaker: Projectionist (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: She gave up the possibility of survival, her dream of touching the stars. And instead, dragged her broken body onwards to share in this madness with you.
rows.speaker: Projectionist (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: We all know how that ended. So please, enjoy this documentary: The Herald of Death's Bloodbath.
rows.speaker: Projectionist (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: While the crazy Supplicant Marcus Antali was drenching Dovebrook in blood as part of his deranged art, a dying girl and her imagenae friend tried desperately to create a miracle!
rows.speaker: Projectionist (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: The Starblazer materialized from your Wishpower, and smashed {RUBY_B#Herald of Death}that frenzied plant{RUBY_E#} into pieces.
rows.speaker: Projectionist (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: As the winner, she made her wish: for Aha to take her real life, her name, her memories, and her dream of Trailblazing the cosmos, and give them all to you.
rows.speaker: Projectionist (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: For her part, she would watch you and the Astral Express soar into the sky, while she remained on this planet forever, and with all her regrets, turn to ashes.
rows.speaker: Projectionist (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Come, impostor. Open this door, add the final stroke to the second act of this artwork.
rows.speaker: Projectionist (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: It is completely quiet behind this door...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: "Let's just call it... a long-overdue compensation."
There's no turning back if we open this door and leave the sanatorium.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: And we're not planning to return anyway, right?
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: It's just... Can we really win?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: And what if I hold you back?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Then I'll drag you forward.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: ...Don't be ridiculous.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: You're not the one who wished for my birth or to take your place. From the moment I was born, I have only heard you wish to be your own person.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: Let me build up the little faith you need: I believe Himeko will go further than anyone else.
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: If you don't believe in yourself in this moment...
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: ...then believe in the future "me."
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: ...Thank you. I won't let myself be afraid anymore.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: This battle is not about winners or losers. As we speak, the Herald of Death is freely turning Dovebrook upside down. Someone has to stop him.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Let's go then!
rows.speaker: Motoko (?)

rows.text: There's one thing I still don't understand.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: No matter how many times I painted the Starblazer, I never finished.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I think it may be because uncertainty still plagues you.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Becoming a Navigator, leading the Express across a sea of stars... You haven't seen these things with your own eyes, and you can't imagenate them either.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Then how did we defeat the Herald of Death?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Because we have each other.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: And whenever I close my eyes, I see you becoming the Navigator.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: And the Astral Express readying for departure, its lights illuminating the dark.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: I've tried all the medicines...
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Go join the Phantasmoon Games!
rows.speaker: Doctor (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Where are you going? Shouldn't Navigators always know the right way?
Fine by me, if you want to keep wasting time. Let's go over these 42 different reactions.
42! Golly! Did you actually believe me? Just kidding, there are only these two. Go again if you don't believe me.
Beneath your feet are countless paths, and they are surrounded by nameless stars.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: You saw a path no one had ever trod before.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Then you set off on it.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Keep moving forward, and the obstacles that once felt impossible to conquer will soon be behind you. And along the way, you'll find companions who are just like you.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: This is the sight I see every day, and it has never lost its clarity.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: I would like to see it too.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: You will.
rows.speaker: Motoko & Himeko

rows.text: A surprise? But today's not my birthday.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: How do I look in your vision? Do I look the same?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Exactly the same.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Fifteen years, Motoko.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I never imagined we would reunite in this manner.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: How about the Phantasmoon Games?
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Phantasmoon Games!
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Look! The last of the Graphia clan!
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Drowning in the absurd dream of Trailblazing!
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Quick, go join the Phantasmoon Games!
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Well, it's been fifteen years! You must have walked a long way.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Yes! So long that I learned to repair machines, brew coffee, take care of my juniors, and fight with everything I have...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What do I care about...?
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Join the Phantasmoon Games?
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: I've tried all the medicines...
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Go join the Phantasmoon Games!
rows.speaker: Doctor (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Down to just a few months of life...
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: How about the Phantasmoon Games?
rows.speaker: Doctor (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: She's going to join the Phantasmoon Games!
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: Will she get what she wants? Or...
rows.speaker: Patient (played by Asat Pramad)

rows.text: The pain and hardship of the past, Himeko has left all of that behind. The road ahead is yours to walk on your own two feet.
So long that I became like you, and even deceived a Lord Ravager with a talent for disguise.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's not time to stop yet. So, will you keep going?
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Let's go then, Himeko.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Let me be your strength too.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Anything you wish to say?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What's going on here?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Eh? Did I make a mistake? It was Himeko who survived fifteen years ago, not Motoko?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Hopefully you like this answer... even if it does make you look laughable.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: No! How can— My daughter, you're alive!?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: This makes me even more interested in you.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Thousands of years ago, I struck a train down from the same starry sky.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Fifteen years ago, I sped back toward Planarcadia, and all I could see was a speck of light rising from the horizon.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I raised my hand and aimed right at it. Just two shots, "bang, bang," and it would fall once more, never to fly again.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: But you did no such thing.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Indeed. I watched it pass through the atmosphere, leaving a long streak of light in the night sky.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Why?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Just 'cause. Thought it might be fun.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Do you understand? I destroyed the Express once, but I also spared it in a moment of whimsy. Whether the Express is unscathed or destroyed... I decide its fate.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: No. You're wrong.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I also wondered why I should be the one to find the Express once. What does it really mean?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The answer is very simple: the person that found the Express, happened to be me.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The meteor showed the way to the Express from the moment it fell. And for a thousand years, it waited for someone to follow the trail and find it.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Even if two, three, or even ten thousand years passed, and I was no more, the Express was still going to be found and returned to the sky.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You're not a god that decides fate. You're just an obsessed egomaniac.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Right you are! All gods ARE obsessed egomaniacs!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: My guesses were wrong, but the game isn't over yet. Shall we take another step forward? Fill in the remaining blank space in this painting?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Round three, question three. Are you ready?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: The coast where the Tower of Infinity slumbered, the place from which the Express set off once more...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Or as I frequently call it: Where Repeated Mistakes Begin.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: So, how does it feel being back on old stomping grounds?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: It's just a shame you are my traveling companion.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Better traveling with me, than traveling alone.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: The Bloodstained Games have no winners. You imagenated your mechatrons, but the remaining Wishpower can't create the audience, much less support a long journey.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Leading us to the third question: How exactly did you cure the Weathering Curse?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You're still beating around the bush? Even now?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Have I ever deviated from the topic at hand?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad
