rows.text: Three blanks, corresponding to three secrets. They seem to point to me, but they really just conceal your true intentions.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Who left the Starblazer's blueprints on the Express? Who met Himeko and Motoko here? How did THEY cure the irreversible Weathering Curse?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You have many questions, but none about your so-called "daughter."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Your real interest is in Aha.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The truth from fifteen years ago is key to figuring out: When the Phantasmoon Games are compromised, what form THEY will descend in, and how THEY plan to intervene.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: So, I guessed right? THEY appeared and ignited the Astral Express?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Stop, the game's over then. You set the rules: a secret for a secret.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You didn't take my trump card.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Yes, but I took mine.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Unfortunately, I wasn't the one who met Aha. The answer you were looking for never existed.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That's what THEY said when {RUBY_B#Aha}THEY{RUBY_E#} gave me the gift.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Lost in thought again?
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: You beat the Herald of Death, but you're not happy.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: I just... Well, I'm not sure how to put it.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Because I'm {RUBY_B#fading away}leaving{RUBY_E#} soon?
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Once the Express reignites and takes off, there won't be any Wishpower in the vacuum, and imagenae will die out. This is the best {RUBY_B#gift}outcome{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: But...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: If I just set off like this, I know it'll haunt my dreams forever.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Thinking back on it, my dream... was built on someone else's sacrifice.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: If you feel scared, just look up.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Up there are the same stars we gazed at together for countless nights.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: You'll see all those sights in my stead, and experience all those stories as wonderful and strange... as imagenae.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: You've known all along, haven't you? So be brave, and stop this talk about sacrifices.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: I give my life to conquer the land that trapped us here.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: You have to go alone, dummy.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: What did you say when you created me? I quote: "If I die, I want to die where the stars are within reach."
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: When the Phantasmoon is full again, I will be there as I have promised.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I will come back with so many stories to tell you.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: So, deal? If you can't find me to share your stories, then tell them to the moon, like a Mourning Actor.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: The moon's shadow said this while giving me my gift.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: "Let's just call it a long-overdue compensation."
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: "It's time we set off once more, Akivili."
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: So, it was the "self-portrait" that saw Aha?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You placed a bet with a fake chip?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You call it a "challenge," but it's really just a waste of time for you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: This is a blow, I have to admit. Just a little one, but a blow.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Though if you don't have the answer, then I can execute Destruction without a shred of guilt.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You're wrong, again... This little test was your last chance to find your way back.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Interesting. You... were giving me a chance?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Even after falling so far as to become a Lord Ravager, I still wished to give the former Navigator a chance to turn back.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But this journey has convinced me: You are not some wayward Nameless. You are just... another enemy trying to dishonor the Express.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And to enemies, I only respond in one way.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Destroy me...? Could you really?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I saw right through your tricks, Lord Ravager.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You summoned the apocalypse, and transformed a thousand times, and created scenes from the past to confuse me. But in the end...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You just use reality as a canvas to imagenate the uncertain into truth.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You used people's Wishpower to imagenate that impending {RUBY_B#Demon Capital}future{RUBY_E#} born of their fears.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And using the same trick, you imagenated versions of yourself that could exist in different places.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But when {RUBY_B#you are defeated}another possibility is observed by others{RUBY_E#}, it crushes the imagenated lie, and your ability loses its effect instantly.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And what will you do about it, stuck as you are in the World in Canvas?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Even if you summon the feeble Starblazer, and do your best to crash into the space, you will never escape.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Escape? Who said anything about escaping?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Gravity does not only trap people on the ground. It also drags the stars toward each other. Have you, a former Navigator, really forgotten the Nameless distress signal?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: How they use massive collisions to simulate the gravity wave frequency used by the Express to warp jump? Not even imagenated spaces can block out a signal like that.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: My companions have known your secret for a while. In a minute or so, you might see your scheme start to fall apart.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Or is it seconds, not minutes?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Oho! Nicely done. But you have a really terrible habit.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Does becoming a Navigator mean always facing danger on your own? Well, since this game of ours is ending soon...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Can you guess how many people I have lined up to play the same game?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Go on, you have one chance to guess the answer. The probability of you stopping me is...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Zero.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: What exactly are you planning to do?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Who says the great destroyer of Elation came to Planarcadia to kill Aha?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You are not my target... THEY are not my target... Shall I officially announce my plan?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: In the Name of Terminus, [Trailblazer]'s journey ends here.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: "Ignite the Express's Engine" is definitely a tad too dramatic if Himeko just wants us to rescue survivors with the Express.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: What was she implying?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: If Asat Pramad was close by, then he would have discovered any clues Himeko left behind.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: So... her message seems pretty standard, but only we'll know what she really means because we're the Nameless?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Something about the engine of the Express? Has Himeko mentioned something of this sort in previous journeys? This may be the key.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Well... I kind of zone out whenever Himeko starts talking about warps and calibrating coordinates and all that...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Power of Remembrance, activate!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: A-ha! I remember now. We were back in Penacony...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Talking about the Charmony Festival, and Himeko said: "The Family sent a music box as an 'Invitation'"... And then she said...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Some time ago, at Perdido Station...
"But the box that was sent to us was slightly unusual... The music it played had off-key notes in the background."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: "I recorded these dissonant notes, and they were a perfect match with the gravity wave frequency when the Express made its warp jump. Also, the Express engine's spatial curvature was its encryption key."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: How much could she say if Asat Pramad was with her?
"...A distress call method regularly used by the Nameless."
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I remember now! Pearl said something similar not too long ago...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: "A conflict broke out between Miss Himeko and an entity suspected to be Asat Pramad... a gravitational wave effect caused by a giant mass was observed..."
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Himeko is hinting that we should use the Gravity Probe on the Express to receive her signal!
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That's exactly it!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: If that's the case, we need to get ready as soon as possible!
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It'll take some time to clear the passage to the Express. Sunday, do you have a way to contact the conductor?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The distance does not pose a problem for tuning. However, my birds must first lock onto the conductor as their target.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I will do my best. Please excuse me for a moment.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I received a message that Silver Wolf has arrived at Pearluxe Tower.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Together with Pearl, she'll repair the communication systems across Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Then, with Graphia's assistance, they'll attempt to re-enact the ritual from a millennium ago, folding all of Planarcadia back into the canvas — the most extreme measure of protection.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: How's the situation here?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: We're making progress!
Worried about Silver Wolf?
Very good.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: No. I trust her.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Go ahead and do your part. As for the rest, leave it to me.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Let me open my senses...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Good news, everyone! The conductor is safe and sound.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: My bird has located them. I am able to share what the conductor is seeing.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: A moment, please, while I inform them of the situation...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So, Asat Pramad is a Lord Ravager that observes and imagenates possibilities.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That explains why I could never land a blow on him.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: When people saw the Lord Ravager's descent, they were gripped with fear, despair, and everything else that comes with an apocalyptic end. Those very emotions fed this catastrophe and made a possibility become reality.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Himeko said we need to observe another possibility for this apocalypse to be overwritten. "Observe another possibility"... How do we do that?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Build a crowd, then defeat Asat Pramad in front of them. That's the easiest way.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: But he'll just create hundreds of clones to hide behind, and no one will be able to lay a finger on him. That's another of his tricks by manipulating possibilities.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: So, we don't actually have any way of defeating that old dicehead!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: A few moments later...
Any progress?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yes. The conductor says they have locked on to a weak gravitational wave, and are decoding it...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Pom-Pom sure is glad that everybody's okay!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Conductor! We missed you too!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Pom-Pom received Himeko's message! Repeating it now...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: "The source of Asat Pramad's power is fear. He exploits people's fears to imagenate future possibilities."
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: "When another possibility is observed, this apocalypse will be overwritten."
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: And! And also...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: "Each and every one of us Nameless is making it to the next stop!" This part is the conductor's heartfelt wish!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: We're coming, Himeko!
Who says we're out of options?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: If we somehow witness all his {RUBY_B#clones}possibilities{RUBY_E#}, then he would collapse into just one being due to the effect of observation.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I will activate the formation plume I've set up all over the arcadia, then use the vision of the Reignbow Spiritus "Kālacakra Skyplume"!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: General, do you require my cooperation like during SparxiCon?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "...Each reading drives the murky future toward a definite outcome, a collapsed quantum state, even if that outcome isn't to one's liking."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: "...The 'Eye of Īśvara' would transcend mere sight and permeate throughout this realm. The Kālacakra Skyplume would predict the future of all beings at tens of billions of instances per second."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: That's right, Mr. Sunday. I would like you to expand the range of your "tuning"...
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: You mean to determine the future of Asat Pramad through observation? But... as I recall, as your observation expands, it will anchor the fate of this world.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Observation is for [Trailblazer] to worry about.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I want you to become "my eyes" and look for me.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: The fate Asat Pramad imagenated is imminent, and there is no path for the future in it. Only "īśvara," only observers with sufficient strength and personal freedom have what it takes to make choices that trace the paths to our future.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I also need a place with a good vantage point... Something like a towering structure.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: How confident are you in this plan succeeding, General?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Even if the chance of success is only a coin toss, once I enter the fray myself... I always treat it as a "one-hundred-percent certainty."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I'll fight by your side too, even if there is only half a chance of success.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Me? You're leaving the observation to me?
I will do all I can to ensure you two remain connected through "tuning."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Then, Dan Heng, March, and I will clear the passages as soon as possible, to ensure the Express can depart.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: And myself, [Trailblazer], and General Yao Guang will force the collapse of Asat Pramad's clones, granting us a way to his true form.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Thank you, Sunday. Before you boarded the Express, you said that you didn't understand Trailblazing. And yet, you have fought alongside us in the most dangerous moments of our journey.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: No, Mr. Yang, I should be the one thanking all of you. Before boarding the Express, I was just a traveler looking for answers.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You all taught me to Trailblaze and walk the stars. To hold fast to the hands of those around me when facing difficulties. It is my honor to be able to provide assistance.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You really look like one of the Nameless now.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Thank you too, General Yao Guang. The Express will meet you as soon as we rescue Himeko!
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: And that's when we'll defeat Asat Pramad together!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: And when we do bring Himeko home, each and every one of us will be accounted for as well.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: [Trailblazer], you still have time. Go and say your goodbyes to your friends before we set off. Meet me at the entrance when you're ready.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Are you ready?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Before we set off, there's something I'd like you to keep safe for me, [Trailblazer]. Please hold on to my strategy pouch.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: What's inside?
Our future destinies.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: When should I open it?
Open it when you are in need of the Hunt.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Remember when we were at SparxiCon? And you saw the Weal and Woe Lots hanging over me?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I'd like you to keep your eyes on me as much as possible.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Thirty years ago, I used the Deca-Light Reflection Barrier to divine the tides of battle for the Fanghu. But in a moment of blind arrogance, I turned my back on what destiny had revealed, and dared to wield the Reignbow Spiritus to twist the very threads of causality.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: But karma was on the way to punish me. That day, I became entangled with the barrier at a single point, left to drift endlessly through time and space. A healer named this unusual condition "Temporal Dislocation."
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Put simply, there's always a chance that I could suddenly disappear at any moment. If I am not observed for even a second, I may disappear.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Is there no way to reverse it?
And that is why you need me observing you.
I restrain myself with the Nexus Sapientiae forged by the Yuque Artisanship Commission. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I remember. But you commanded me not to tell you what they said.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: There's been so much going on lately... I don't really remember.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I remember. I'll do my best not to glance at your head.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: No, I want the opposite this time.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: We can't afford a single mistake in this operation. You must keep an eye on me always, no matter the fate that I'm anchored to.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I had already decided my fate when I set foot in this world. You are only a witness, not the one wielding the blade.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I'm afraid you must get past it, if you want to reach that tower.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It spotted us!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Fret not, I will protect you.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Himeko and another me had a bet on how far you would get.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: What if we made a bet too? On... whether Himeko is living or dead!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Never fight fate... because it fights back!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Wait, that means...
Asat Pramad, your Elation is just supreme idiocy.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: That thing over there... What is that?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I've seen it at Star Rail FEST. Likely a device that collects people's Wishpower.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: [Trailblazer] has courageously challenged an ancient leviathan of the Cindearth Age...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: ...and {M#his}{F#her} chosen weapon is a standard Planarcadian "ambience prop"!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: As I said, {M#he}{F#she} is peak entertainment!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: At last, the long-awaited prelude: Monster VS Protagonist!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I'm sick of this guy's trifling gimmicks.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: We're here. Get ready, Sunday.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Careful. Asat Pramad just appeared above you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Smart of you to lead a Xianzhou General to her death.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: How honorable and entertaining it would be to challenge the demon lord and save the world alone. But yes, two is better than one.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Still, I was not expecting a diviner. To think I should have the honor of meeting the Divine Foresight, bane of Phantylia. What can she do for you? Reveal your victory odds? Predict your weal and woe?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Whatever she divines, I will block its path. What will you do now?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Then I, a diviner that never grants an audience to anyone, will teach you a lesson...
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Asat Pramad, a general and a diviner have completely different duties. A general breaks formations from behind, and a diviner destroys them from the front!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: And did you say you will block every path I divine? Sorry, but creating paths where there are none is the expertise of Trailblazers.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Now, shall I read your fortune?
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: See your myriad {RUBY_B#clones}possibilities{RUBY_E#} condense, until eventually, only one remains: Defeat!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: I... see it!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: So this insight... is what the eye of The Hunt has to offer?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: ...Good, I see it too!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Asat Pramad, your fate is sealed.
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: Haha... HAHAHA! What a brilliant reversal!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Now this is the resistance I have been looking for! Exhausting all possibilities, plotting every scheme, just hurling everything at me. In short, Elation!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: How unfortunate that this coming, perfect apocalypse will not be seen by you, General Yao Guang.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I see the rope that tethered your existence here has snapped. I do not believe we will meet again in this lifetime.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I have nothing left to give... [Trailblazer], please, take Asat Pramad to his fated defeat!
rows.speaker: Yao Guang

rows.text: General!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Pity. You were so close.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: She put her life on the line for you to have this sliver of a chance. Just like Himeko. Don't let their sacrifices come to nothing.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You know, [Trailblazer], it's actually heartbreaking that those clones are gone. But she did deliver you here to me—
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: [Trailblazer], don't be afraid.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Trust that I will always be by your side.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Keep walking.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko—!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (A beach? What is this place...?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Himeko went that way earlier? I need to catch up...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Himeko... Everyone... Where are you...?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: "Let's just call it a long-overdue compensation."
rows.speaker: Signals From Afar

rows.text: "It's time we set off once more, Akivili."
rows.speaker: Signals From Afar

rows.text: Oh, there you are, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...Himeko! You're okay! Thank goodness!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What is this place?
What happened on the battlefield?
Come on, let's find the others.
The Express...? What is this place?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It's a scene from my memories. Fifteen years ago, I encountered the Astral Express for the first time on this beach.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What just happened? All I remember is you protecting me amidst the chaos.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: But when I opened my eyes again, I was already in this place...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Are you scared? Worried you've lost?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: No, I wouldn't have such thoughts.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: That's right. It's not over yet.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: March, Dan Heng... Where is everyone?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: We have to get back to the fight somehow. We can't keep everyone waiting.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Let's go, Himeko. Whatever it takes, we're getting out of here together!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Himeko...?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'm sorry, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I can't go with you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What...?
I understand. You have many questions... About the battle, about me, and about the Express's crash site...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I didn't expect it to appear in this manner either.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Haven't you figured it out yet? This frozen moment in time... is your very own creation.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In the moment I embraced you, I guess the Stellaron heard my final wish.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Final... wish?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I promised someone that when the moon over my hometown was full again, I would go back to see her, to let her know I had made the most of this borrowed life, and found companions I could trust with all my heart.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Alright, it's a deal. When I return from the World in Canvas, you can make us... um, let Shush make us some coffee. Then we'll settle in and listen to your story.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It's a shame... I'll have to take a rain check on that coffee.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But at least, I still have the chance to honor a promise from long ago.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I know...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (say "her" name)
The "her" you're talking about... is Motoko, right?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'm so glad to hear you say her name. It means she'll always be remembered by someone.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Even if the universe forgets, as long as someone still remembers her name, our trailblazing will never end.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But, as the navigator, it's not just her promise I have to keep... I have to honor my promise to all of you, and to you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: [Trailblazer]...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: This time, you must set out on your own.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's all over. A lost navigator has reached his final destination.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And with that, the Astral Express has taken down another Lord Ravager.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...The Phantasmoon Courtyard?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: A terrifying enemy is near, but you stand alone, helpless. How often have you been in such a predicament... Protagonist?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I'm used to it.
This is how trailblazing expeditions always end, no? Don't worry... as the former {RUBY_B#Isee}navigator{RUBY_E#} myself, I may provide you with some instruction.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Just as Akivili instructed me, and I instructed Falcon Amundsen.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Hmm, perhaps "instruction" is too formal a word. Young people these days can't stand such formality.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: How about we make it a bit friendlier, you quiz me instead?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Next, you can ask me questions... Eight of them...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: About me, about Aha, about Akivili, about the future of the cosmos, about you even... I'll answer anything you ask.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Are you really that kind?
Because once eight questions are done, you're dead.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Did you forget? We are the only two Supplicants with a chance of winning the Phantasmoon Games!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Why eight questions?
Because the die happened to land on eight...because there are eight Supplicants in the Games.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Or perhaps because we first met in Amphoreus... another "8"! Hahaha!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: I'm not interested in playing a dumb trivia game.
You're not interested in stories and secrets? That's unfortunate.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Of course, this universe also has a button reserved for you.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: But let me remind you, this is the last time we will speak so openly.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: (Think about Asat Pramad's offer)
(Is this guy actually serious?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Himeko hasn't escaped yet, and there's no news from the Express. I should try to delay him for as long as possible if we want to have any chance of winning.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Why would I believe a Lord Ravager?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hm. Looks like you're not so opposed to my offer either.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: How about we add a wildcard to this boring trivia game then: Give your answers to the die you're holding.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Die?
Roll the die. If your roll is a critical success, you get to uncover my deepest secret. I will answer every question, even if it works against me.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: And if the roll is bad?
I still answer, but only in half-truths. It shouldn't pose any problem for our protagonist, you can effortlessly distinguish truth from deception.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: And if the roll succeeds but isn't a critical success?
I'll share a candid truth... though it won't necessarily be the whole truth.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: How do I know you'll play fairly?
Didn't General Yao Guang bind me just now? Hahaha! You should really trust her strength!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Besides, it's been a long time since I've just offered myself up to the chessboard of fate.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: How exciting to have every outcome based on pure probability!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: And now, let's get started!
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: ...Another turning point in destiny. We meet again.
For the Express to begin its journey once more, Himeko reached the end of hers...
Get lost.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: This isn't the end.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Eight days ago, you arrived with the Astral Express at Planarcadia.
Eight hours ago, Asat Pramad appeared. Eight minutes ago, you declared war on him.
And eight seconds ago, you lost.
In eight seconds, Himeko will sacrifice her life.
In eight minutes, you will return to the battlefield. In eight hours, a god's great hammer will fall.

In eight days, a paradise will collapse under its own weight, a beast will begin its sacred feast, a divine infant will fall to the mortal world. With its first cry, it will usher in an era of "madness" for the entire cosmos...
And a god will retreat into hiding forever, their laughter heard no more.
This is the path I have walked, and one of countless possibilities. But that doesn't matter.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: What's important is that it was born from the wish Himeko made to the Stellaron, and it only leads to one end: failure.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: Are you... willing to accept such a future?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: What a shame. You still fail to understand what I'm saying...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: I'm asking [Trailblazer], who is still on the path of the Trailblaze: Are you willing to accept such a future?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: I'll never accept it.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Then you know what to do. So many others have made the same decision.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: Make a wish to the Stellaron. Let your wish replace hers.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: Somewhere along this journey, you've already found it.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: ...Each and every one of us Nameless is making it to the next stop.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: And all the {RUBY_B#Preservation}promises{RUBY_E#}, {RUBY_B#The Hunt}oaths{RUBY_E#}, {RUBY_B#Harmony}dreams{RUBY_E#}, and {RUBY_B#Remembrance}pacts{RUBY_E#}...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I'm not leaving a single one behind.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: As it should be.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: I made the same choice once... and lost everything because of it. But you have to get used to loss before you can move on.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: Set forth once more, Akivili. Our paths will cross eventually...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: And when that day comes, I will personally bring your journey to its end.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] from the Future?

rows.text: Yes, I'm back.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko, that outfit looks so cool! You really look the part of a navigator now!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Just like I said, the giant robot was right.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: But, [Trailblazer], are you okay? Just now...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That was the Stellaron inside you, wasn't it?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I don't know what happened, but I'm sure {M#he}{F#she} took a lot of the heat for me in that battle.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And thank you, everyone.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Sunday, I'd like to have a proper chat with you, as the navig—
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Children, I'm not dead yet...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Do you hear the laughter of the people? They are leaving the ruins and setting off once more.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The Wishpower cast upon you has dissipated. Your Bloodstained Games... are over.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: After all this, I'm sure you wouldn't want to call me "Father" anymore.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Heh... but being your "Father"... has been a true pleasure.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: We did it, we won.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Oh, really...? Is that what you think, "protagonist"?
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Then you'll just have to wait and see.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Of all the possibilities you glimpsed, did you ever see one where you lost?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I've seen more than you can possibly imagine.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Look forward to what's to come, "protagonist."
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: The tremors of the Stellaron will shift the cosmos's fate onto a different trajectory.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Even if the Stellaron distorts my wish, I will rewrite it.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Then I shall await with anticipation.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: What a magnificent strike. Pegana's Legacy...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: When it first embarked on its journey, the stars were still brand new. Like... a die thrown high in the air, yet to land.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Wait, something's not right...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The cracks in the earth are spreading... How is this possible...?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The husk of "the Voracity"... is stirring?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hahahaha...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: You have defeated me, and won your reward: the chance to save this world.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: That is, if... you can make it out of THEIR maw with everyone still breathing.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Good luck...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Now, run.
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: And the Astral Express readying for departure, its lights illuminating the dark.
rows.speaker: Signals From Afar

rows.text: Beneath your feet are countless paths, and they are surrounded by nameless stars.
rows.speaker: Signals From Afar

rows.text: You saw a path no one had ever trod before.
rows.speaker: Signals From Afar

rows.text: Then you set off on it.
rows.speaker: Signals From Afar

rows.text: This is the sight I see every day,
rows.speaker: Signals From Afar

rows.text: and it has never lost its clarity.
rows.speaker: Signals From Afar

rows.text: I would like to see it too.
rows.speaker: Signals From Afar

rows.text: [Trailblazer], don't be afraid.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Trust that I will always be by your side.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Keep walking.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko—!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (A beach? What is this place...?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Himeko went that way earlier? I need to catch up...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Himeko... Everyone... Where are you...?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You have to go alone, dummy.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: What did you say when you created me? I quote: "If I die, I want to die where the stars are within reach."
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: But now, you have everything you need to set off. Even {RUBY_B#the future}time{RUBY_E#}, the one thing you were missing, is now in your hands.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: But... the Weathering Curse can't be healed. How did you do it...?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Sorry... I made a decision on my own while you were asleep.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Aha... appeared?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: No, THEY didn't answer us... This Phantasmoon Games has no winner.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: But I saw a shadow peek out from behind the moon.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: It said, "Apologies, I am not 'the Elation,' so I cannot reward you in THEIR stead."
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: "But, a Phantasmoon Games with only bloodshed and no miracles wouldn't be very satisfying."
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: "So, I can offer up the strength I've accumulated to grant you a wish. Unfortunately, it's a limited wish, so it can't make all your dreams come true. But it should be enough to offer some small assistance."
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: What... exactly was the wish?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I made a wish to the Phantasmoon, in exchange for something.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: An exchange...?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: An exchange of Himeko's and Motoko's destinies... not for a minute, but for a lifetime.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: The brand of Destruction can never be erased, but it can be passed on to someone willing to bear it.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: To think the answer was so simple... So that's why Murata Hiro left nothing behind... He was a kind person, just like you.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: No... This can't be true!
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: This is so unfair! I don't want my wishes to be granted at the cost of someone else's life!
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: We made a promise! You were the one who was supposed to embark on a new journey, to fly to the stars and see all those worlds for me! We made a promise!
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: That's right... if you were awake, your wish would've been clear: "For Motoko to have a fulfilling life."
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: But if I left you behind to travel the stars alone, I wouldn't be the "ideal navigator" we talked about.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: You nurtured me with stories of the Astral Express, you sketched me into existence, and you brought me to life. The "you" that you never imagined would grow up, became a truly remarkable adult in the end.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: I'm the grown-up you, a navigator who, despite never having taken a single step, has already experienced so much. And a "Himeko" like that would surely pass on the hope of "continuing the journey" to the next generation, wouldn't she?
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: So, don't be sad. My Trailblazing ends here, but it also begins here.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: No, I won't accept this!
I just... I just wanted you to see the world outside, to see the starry sky I told you about...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I'm here now. I can see it.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Do you hear that, Himeko? When the urge to "go and see for yourself, no matter what" swells up inside you, your fire has already ignited the Express's engine.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Go, Himeko. Start up the Express, walk a path without the Aeons' protection, and become your own god...
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Then, grant me this wish: When you've become like me, return here with all your stories.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Motoko, when the Phantasmoon is full again, I will be there as I have promised!
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I will come back with so many stories to tell you.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: So, deal? If you can't find me to share your stories, then tell them to the moon, like a Mourning Actor.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: Now, let's get on the Express together. As we travel through the atmosphere and fly toward the stars...
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: I will become a star and watch over you forever.
rows.speaker: Motoko

rows.text: So... are you going to say goodbye to us too, just like Motoko...?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: If I could, I'd wish for this moment to come a little later, too.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But that's how it is for the Nameless. The journey always begins and ends when you least expect it.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Don't worry too much. I just... have to depart for the next stop.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But the Crew can't keep on Trailblazing without you!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Are you really going to accept this ending?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: No, I'll never accept this plan!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I used to be afraid of goodbyes like this, too.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Whenever that happens, I just look up at the sky. Up there are the same stars we gazed at together for countless nights.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I know you'll see all those sights in my stead, and experience all those stories as wonderful and strange... as imagenae.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You understand all of this, don't you? So be brave, and stop this talk about sacrifices.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Tell March for me... if there's anything she likes in my wardrobe, she can have it.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...She has enough clothes as it is.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Tell Dan Heng that he'll have more on his plate, so he shouldn't try to carry everything all by himself.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...I'll help him.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Tell Welt... I really wanted to go with him to his homeland... but I never thought... I'd be the one to step off the Express first. I'm sorry.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...I'll tell him.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: And tell Pom-Pom... If no one's going to use the coffee machine or the beans, just toss them, make space for future passengers.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I... will.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: And one more thing, about Sunday... Tell him not to be so uptight all the time. Plenty of people come and go on the Express. He should feel free to do as he pleases, not feel so burdened.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And finally, [Trailblazer]... you're the one I'm most worried about.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Have you been satisfied with your journey so far?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You don't have to say it. Keep the answer in your heart.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You still have a long journey of Trailblazing ahead of you, so walk on. Walk this path without the Aeons' protection, and become your own god...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And then, you can grant my wish: Come back here and tell me all about your amazing stories.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: If you can't find me, just look up at the stars.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And as always, I'll be there to light up the entire night sky for you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: By the way, I have a ninth question.
